newsitem.title: CHINA: HK launches public consultation on corporate tax.
newsitem.headline: HK launches public consultation on corporate tax.

text.p: The Hong Kong government on Tuesday launched a public consultation exercise as part of a comprehensive review of profits tax.
"The Financial Secretary proposed such a review in his 1997-98 Budget Speech with a view to making our taxation system and business environment more competitive," a government spokesman said.
"On the basis of the review, we will formulate proposals on profits tax for the 1998-99 Budget," he said.
The consultation period will last six weeks, until September 6, 1997.
Corporate profits tax currently stands at 16.5 percent, which the consultation paper noted was the lowest in the region. But tax incentives elsewhere had eroded the gap, it said.

"Obviously we want to ensure that Hong Kong continues to be a premier international business and financial centre in the region. We therefore need to consider whether our competitive edge is still enough or whether changes elsewhere in the region have eroded it to the point that we have to respond and take appropriate action," it said.
Other topics in the paper included tax incentives to encourage research and development, alterations to depreciation, the definition of territorial source and double taxation.

Hong Kong prides itself on having a simple and low tax regime, but has been under pressure from business interests to boost the territory's competitiveness compared with regional rivals, especially in view of Hong Kong's perennial budget surpluses.
